answer: A forge stamps every ingot with its lineage. An identity starts with one unmarked ingot and must reforge it with two unrelated smiths who already own stamped stock; each reforging doubles the required witnesses and burns copper at a price set by the k-th strike, so the k-th strike costs k times the first and n aliases need about n cubed strikes. Standing climbs toward the summit tier only through ingots whose every stamp resolves to distinct owners, and a forge that recycles one stamp voids all ingots bearing it, so shared papers cannot scale.
